title: Cap. X Ultimum Propos. 1.III: the Grace of Christ the Fathers pressed is what Pelagius and Arminius explode as free will’s coercive — Bishop of Salisbury De vera grat. Christi p.60
pass_a_gloss: III. Let us come unto that which remains to be unfolded in this our first proposition; namely, What that grace was which Augustine together with the rest of the Orthodox contended should be acknowledged by Pelagius, and which they pointed out by excellence as the Grace of Christ. But we affirm it was no other than this which Pelagius and Arminius exploded as free will’s coercive. Nor can we depict it in fitter words than it is depicted by the Reverend Bishop of Salisbury, De vera grat. Christi, pag. 60. This, he says, is the true grace which Christian faith acknowledges and believes, by which God gives his laws into our minds, and inscribes them in our hearts; by which, where he requires our will, he himself makes that we will; where he commands to be converted, he makes at once that we are converted; where he demands faith, he makes by his gift that we believe.
pass_b_english: III. What remains in this first proposition: what grace Augustine with the other Orthodox contended Pelagius must acknowledge—and which they named by excellence the Grace of Christ. We affirm it was none other than the grace Pelagius and Arminius explode as free will’s coercive. We cannot paint it in fitter words than the Reverend Bishop of Salisbury (De vera gratia Christi, p. 60): This is the true grace Christian faith owns and believes, by which God gives his laws into our minds and writes them on our hearts; by which, when he requires our will, he himself makes us will; when he bids convert, he makes us convert at once; when he demands faith, by his gift he makes us believe.
source_text: III. Veniamus ad illud quod in hac prima propositione nostra restat explicandum; Qualis nimirum fuerit ea gratia, quam Augustinus una cum reliquis Orthodoxis a Pelagio agnosci contendebant, quamque per excellentiam Gratiam Christi indigitabant. Affirmamus autem, non aliam fuisse quam hanc quam Pelagius et Arminius quasi liberi arbitrii coactivum exploserunt. Non possumus autem eam aptioribus vocabulis depingere, quam depicta est a Reverendo Episcopo Sarisburiensi, De vera grat. Christi, pag. 60. Haec, inquit ille, est vera gratia, quam Christiana fides agnoscit et credit, qua Deus dat leges suas in mentes nostras, et in cordibus nostris inscribit eas; qua ubi requirit voluntatem nostram, facit ipse ut velimus; ubi converti jubet, facit simul ut convertamur; ubi fidem postulat, facit dono suo ut credamus.
